briefing.headline: US-China AI compute sanctions escalate as frontier labs race toward AGI thresholds

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI race has intensified with multiple labs reporting capability jumps in reasoning and agentic systems. Regulatory pressure mounts in both Washington and Brussels while compute access remains the primary bottleneck. Multi-agent security protocols are emerging as critical infrastructure.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI's Orion preview shows 40% gains on agent benchmarks. Anthropic's Claude 4.5 and Google's Gemini 3.0 both launched this week. Meta open-sourced Llama 4 while xAI and DeepSeek released competing 1T parameter models.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for multi-agent, automotive, and BCI environments.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA Blackwell ramp reaches 500k units monthly. Microsoft and Google announced new 100k GPU clusters in Texas and Nevada. TSMC reports 2nm AI chip yields improving ahead of schedule.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will export controls on advanced chips slow China's frontier progress more than they accelerate domestic alternatives?
